title: U.S. House · New York's 22nd District
area: Central New York, including Syracuse and Onondaga County, plus Madison, Oswego and parts of Oneida County.

context.text: Both the Democratic and Republican primaries for this seat were canceled; incumbent John Mannion and Kailee Buller each advanced without appearing on the primary ballot.

summary.text: John Mannion is the Democratic and Working Families Party incumbent, a former high school science teacher and teachers' union president who served in the New York State Senate before winning the 22nd District seat in 2024. He sits on the House Agriculture and Education and Workforce committees and is seeking a second term.

background.text: Born in Syracuse, New York in 1968; his official biography says he was raised on Syracuse's Tipperary Hill and is the grandson of Irish immigrants.
Earned a bachelor's degree in biology from Binghamton University and a master's degree in secondary education from SUNY Oswego.
Spent nearly 30 years teaching high school science, including Advanced Placement Biology and Chemistry, according to his official biography.
Served eight years as president of the West Genesee Teachers' Association, which his official biography says represented about 400 teachers, school nurses and school psychologists.
Lost the 2018 race for the 50th State Senate District to Republican Bob Antonacci, then won the seat in 2020 over Republican Angi Renna.
Served in the New York State Senate from 2020 to 2024, narrowly winning re-election in 2022 after a recount; was the founding chair of the Senate Committee on Disabilities.
According to his official biography, he helped enact New York's Green CHIPS legislation, and as a state senator secured four consecutive cost-of-living increases for Direct Support Professionals.
Won the 2024 Democratic primary and then the general election against Republican incumbent Brandon Williams; took office in January 2025.

Serves on the House Committee on Education and Workforce and the House Committee on Agriculture; his first bill was the Protecting Students with Disabilities Act and he introduced the Science of Reading Act, which passed the House.
Lives in Geddes with his wife, Jennifer, an elementary school teacher; they have three children, according to his official biography.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Agriculture (Commodity Markets, Digital Assets and Rural Development; Conservation, Research and Biotechnology subcommittees) and the Committee on Education and the Workforce in the 119th Congress.

candidates.name: Kailee Buller
candidates.currentRole: Former Chief of Staff to the Secretary of the U.S. Department of Agriculture

summary.text: Kailee Buller is an Auburn native and former federal agriculture official running as the Republican and Conservative nominee. She served as Chief of Staff to Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins from January 2025 until February 2026, after leading two food-industry trade associations. Her campaign is centered on affordability, energy costs and agriculture.

background.text: Born in Auburn, New York, where she grew up in a blue-collar family; her father worked 41 years as a correctional officer at Auburn Correctional Facility and her mother is a nurse, according to her campaign website.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University at Buffalo (a B.A. in political science, per USDA); describes herself as the first in her family to earn a four-year degree.
Served during the first Trump administration as Chief of Staff to the Deputy Secretary of Agriculture and in other leadership roles at USDA.
Served as President and CEO of the National Oilseed Processors Association and the Edible Oil Producers Association.
Appointed by Virginia Governor Glenn Youngkin as the 8th Congressional District representative on the Virginia Board of Agriculture and Consumer Services.

Served as USDA Chief of Staff to Secretary Brooke Rollins from January 2025; her campaign website describes the role as overseeing a $200 billion operation with 100,000 employees. She left the department on February 19, 2026.

Her campaign website says she lives with her husband, Eric, and their three young children, and that she is running to restore affordability, strengthen public trust and put Central New York families first.

priorities.text: Affordability and jobs, focused on lowering everyday costs such as groceries, gas, childcare and housing.
Energy and utility costs, opposing what she calls Albany's climate mandates and supporting an "all-of-the-above" energy policy.
Agriculture policy, drawing on her USDA experience to focus on cutting regulations and supporting farmers and rural communities.

positions.summary: Supports repealing New York's climate mandates and advancing an "all-of-the-above" energy policy, saying state climate policy has driven up utility costs.
Supports policies that encourage housing development, cut regulations and make it easier for first-time buyers to enter the market.
Says New York is the highest-taxed state in the nation and criticizes higher taxes and spending as funding what she calls politicians' pet projects.
